Here's a firmer version that remains professional and is something your attorney is less likely to object to:

> Grant,
>
> I have already provided proof that the payment was made. This matter has been addressed, and I will not discuss it further.
>
> If you believe there is a legitimate issue, you may contact Detective Megan Valentin directly. Do not contact me regarding this matter.
>
> Effective immediately, I am directing you to cease all unwanted communication with me. Your repeated emails and attempts to contact me after this notice are unwanted and will be documented. Any further harassment or unnecessary contact will be reported to law enforcement, and I will pursue all available legal remedies, including seeking a protective order if necessary.
>
> Do not contact me again except through legal counsel or as otherwise required by law.

This version clearly sets a boundary and states what you intend to do if the contact continues, without making claims that could be interpreted as inflammatory or speculative.

If your attorney may review this, it's generally better to keep the message brief, factual, and avoid profanity or threats. A calm, clear boundary is often more effective than an emotional response.

You could send:

> Grant,
>
> I have already provided documentation showing that the payment was made. I will not continue discussing this matter with you.
>
> If you believe there is any legitimate issue that requires attention, you may direct all future communications regarding this matter to Detective Megan Valentin. Please contact her directly rather than contacting me.
>
> Going forward, I am requesting that you cease contacting me directly except as required by law or through the appropriate legal channels. I consider your repeated communications after this request to be unwanted contact, and I am maintaining records of all communications.
>
> Do not contact me again.

One important note: only include Detective Megan Valentin's phone number or email if she has actually authorized you to direct him to her. Otherwise, your attorney may instead prefer that you direct him to your attorney or simply state that all future communication should occur through legal channels. That approach is often cleaner from a legal standpoint.

Here's a shorter, direct version:

> Grant,
>
> I have already provided proof that the payment was made. This matter is closed.
>
> If you believe there is a legitimate issue, contact your attorney or Detective Megan Valentin, who has been made aware of your ongoing harassment.
>
> Do not contact me again. Any further communication will be documented and reported to law enforcement as harassment. I will pursue all available legal remedies, including a protective order if necessary. Future communication must go through legal counsel.
